description: Boeing 767-232 Ship 102; bought for Delta in 1982 by its own employees through payroll donations; the museum's signature exhibit inside Hangar Two; FAA MASTER September 2026 still shows Delta Air Lines Inc Atlanta GA

Boeing 747-451; the first 747-400 ever built; ex-Northwest Airlines; outdoor walk-through exhibit and event space known as the 747 Experience; FAA MASTER September 2026 shows Delta Air Lines Inc Atlanta GA
Boeing 757-232; parked outdoors on the museum apron; FAA MASTER September 2026 shows Delta Air Lines Inc Atlanta GA

Delta Ship 41; DC-3-357; restored to 1940 Delta livery and displayed inside Hangar One; the museum runs periodic walk-through tours of it; FAA MASTER September 2026 gives DC3-G202A c/n 3278 year 1940 owner Delta Air Lines Inc Atlanta GA
Outdoor display; FAA MASTER September 2026 registers it to Delta Air Transport Heritage Museum DBA Atlanta GA with c/n 45351 — the museum's own registered airframe
DC-9-51; ex-Delta; tail and rear fuselage section displayed; no longer in the FAA MASTER file which is consistent with a permanently grounded museum exhibit

Forward fuselage and flight deck only; this is c/n 1001 the very first TriStar built; note the N-number N1011 is now held by an unrelated Cessna T210N in California per FAA MASTER September 2026 so the registration is historic not current

Cockpit and nose section only; registration and c/n 01 taken from Aerial Visuals dossier 2229 and NOT independently confirmed — the airframe is out of the FAA register; treat the N-number as unverified
Gull-wing Stinson Reliant displayed inside Hangar One; FAA MASTER September 2026 registers it to Delta Air Transport Heritage Museum Inc Atlanta GA c/n 9755 year 1936

Travel Air 6-B; represents Delta's earliest passenger service; displayed inside Hangar One; FAA MASTER September 2026 shows Curtiss Wright Travel Air 6-B c/n 6B-2040 year 1931 owner Delta Air Lines Inc Atlanta GA

Waco 10 also catalogued by the museum as a Waco 125; the museum describes it as the only aircraft of its kind remaining; displayed inside Hangar One; Aerial Visuals gives c/r NC4546 c/n 1397 but that registration is absent from the September 2026 FAA MASTER file so it is recorded here as an alias only
Small homebuilt biplane in the museum collection per Aerial Visuals dossier 2229; no registration substantiated

REPLICA — full-scale reproduction of the crop-duster that Delta's predecessor Huff Daland Dusters flew; displayed inside Hangar One and identified as a replica in the museum's own material; recorded as a replica not an original airframe
